title: Machine Learning for Ancient Languages: A Survey
institution: Affiliations in the 2023 paper; Oxford publication record verified
primary_evidence: Survey separates restoration, attribution, linguistic analysis, translation and decipherment; translation references were followed to Sumerian and H2KE.
proposed_use: Borrow task taxonomy and interdisciplinary design; evaluate translation as its own task.
limitations: 2023 survey is a starting map, not exhaustive coverage of 2026.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication

title: Neural Decipherment via Minimum-Cost Flow: From Ugaritic to Linear B
authors: Jiaming Luo, Yuan Cao, Regina Barzilay
institution: MIT CSAIL and Google Brain at publication
primary_evidence: 2019 cognate/character-mapping experiments; repository README, datasets and configuration layout inspected.
proposed_use: Use phonological and lexical constraints when representations are uncertain.
limitations: Not passage translation. Historical-language cognate accuracy does not validate Pahlavi meaning. Old dependencies; root license not verified.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication

title: Electronic Babylonian Literature
primary_evidence: Official project describes a corpus of scholarly editions, translations and lexical indexing, with fragment matching; public ebl-api source and MIT software license inspected.
proposed_use: Model editions, witnesses, lexical links and source provenance; retrieval should return scholarship rather than unsupported consensus.
limitations: Akkadian/Sumerian project; fragment matching is not a general translation engine. Software license is not a blanket data license.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication

title: Coptic Scriptorium and coptic-nlp
authors: Amir Zeldes and Coptic Scriptorium collaborators
primary_evidence: Documentation exposes original/normalized tokens, lemmas, POS, syntax, translation and translator layers; public processing pipeline inspected at README level.
proposed_use: Keep linguistic representations, English translation and provenance aligned; annotate useful multiword expressions and roles.
limitations: Tools target Coptic. Automatic annotation needs validation in Pahlavi; corpus licenses are component-specific.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication

title: Syntax as a Rosetta Stone: Using Syntactic Structure for In-Context Ancient Language Translation
authors: Paper author list at primary source
primary_evidence: 2026 Coptic experiments add dictionary and verbalized dependency information to LLM prompts; code repository and experiment layout inspected.
proposed_use: Test verified lexical and syntactic evidence with the same base model, including automatic-versus-expert annotations.
limitations: No Pahlavi test; paper acknowledges absent human evaluation and unvalidated metrics. Metric reference-shape concern sent for separate source audit.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication

title: Coptic-French neural translation experiments
institution: Author repository; LREC 2026 workshop listing checked
primary_evidence: Pretrained NMT adapted on biblical parallel text with alternate French translations and book-level test split; public data preparation/experiment/checkpoint references inspected.
proposed_use: Compare translation-specialized adaptation, alternate valid targets and explicit representation choices.
limitations: Bible-domain and automatic-metric results; public books may be present in foundation pretraining. Related-language and architecture effects not isolated.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication

title: Sanskrit Linguistics Web Services
institution: Inria Paris-Rocquencourt and University of Hyderabad, as listed in paper
primary_evidence: COLING 2014 demonstration paper describes interoperable lexicons, morphology, segmentation and dependency analysis with human selection among alternatives.
proposed_use: Constrain possible readings with lexical and grammatical evidence; retain alternative analyses rather than word substitution.
limitations: Sanskrit-specific resources are not directly reusable Pahlavi grammar. Described tools do not demonstrate full Pahlavi translation.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication

title: Towards the First Machine Translation System for Sumerian Transliterations
authors: Ravneet Punia, Niko Schenk, Christian Chiarcos, Emilie Page-Perron
institution: DTU, Amazon, Goethe University, University of Toronto at publication
primary_evidence: 2020 study: 10,147 unique phrase pairs, short administrative material, neural/phrase-based comparisons; linked repository training layout and reported results inspected.
proposed_use: Start with explicit domain/task limits and compare simple transfer baselines; assess whether gains survive longer unfamiliar passages.
limitations: Average 2.8 source tokens limits passage generalization. Paper removed conflicting translations; Pahlavi alternatives must instead be adjudicated. Repository's later corpus update is distinct from paper data.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication

title: Translating Hanja Historical Documents to Contemporary Korean and English
authors: Juhee Son, Jiho Jin, Haneul Yoo, Jin Yeong Bak, Kyunghyun Cho, Alice Oh
primary_evidence: Shared multilingual Transformer uses 359,726 older-Korean parallel pairs plus 14,356 contemporary-Korean and 26,227 English pairs; 45 short samples assessed by six ITKC experts.
proposed_use: Joint English/Farsi supervision and historical-to-modern reference transfer are credible candidates; use domain experts separately from fluency raters.
limitations: Expert evaluation supports a narrow Korean sample, not all directions or Pahlavi. Adding target tasks can also hurt. Public demo does not establish a turnkey training release.
evidence_level: Primary-source research and static inspection; no local replication
